window: Friday 2026-09-25 close -> Sunday 2026-09-27 7:00 AM ET (weekend edition, day 2)
lede: Weekend edition: week in review and week ahead.
geo_headlines: TRUMP PUBLICLY REJECTED IRAN'S HORMUZ PLAN; TEHRAN SAYS IT IS STILL WAITING FOR A FORMAL ANSWER. Outside the White House Trump said "I'm rejecting their deal... that deal would not be acceptable," adding that the US has "total control" of the strait and that 29 ships crossed it the previous day (ABC News, RFE/RL). Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran has seen the remarks but no official reply through mediators, and that any reopening is contingent on Iran's conditions. **All of this came after Friday's settle.**

TEHRAN'S RHETORIC HARDENED OVERNIGHT. President Pezeshkian said Iran no longer trusts talks with Washington; a senior general warned Gulf neighbours the strait stays closed until US economic warfare ends (Al Jazeera). The IRGC Navy's deputy political commander told Fars that Iran would hit US vessels even in the Indian Ocean if fighting resumes. The coverage reviewed reports threats, not new strikes.

WASHINGTON IS TIGHTENING THE ECONOMIC SQUEEZE INSTEAD. Treasury Secretary Bessent said the UAE has stopped all Iranian airline flights and Turkey and Oman halted Mahan Air arrivals, part of a campaign the Journal says reached more than 50 countries. At the UN, Saudi Arabia's foreign minister demanded Hormuz return to pre-February 28 conditions with no transit fees (RFE/RL).

OIL REOPENS TONIGHT HAVING PRICED A DEAL THAT WAS JUST TURNED DOWN. Brent settled $104.32 Friday (-2.14%) and WTI $92.41 (-2.33%) on truce hopes. Energy futures reopen at 6:00 PM ET; the first question is how much of Friday's decline comes back. Trump's claim that tankers are moving is the offsetting argument.

BONDS ENDED THE WEEK WITH A BULL STEEPENER AND A 2026 HIGH IN THE 30-YEAR. Treasury's curve file for Friday: 2-year 4.81% (-6bp), 10-year 5.17% (-1), 20-year 5.54% and 30-year 5.49%, both their highest closes of 2026; 2s10s 36bp from 31. Over the week the nominal 10-year rose 16bp and the real 10-year 15bp, so the breakeven moved one basis point - the price of money, not an inflation scare.

HIKE ODDS EASED FRIDAY AS OIL FELL. CME FedWatch (reporting 9/25, unchanged over the weekend): October hike 64.2%, down from 70.9%; at least one hike by December 91.9%; a 49.8% chance December ends 50bp higher. Cleveland's Hammack warned an inflationary mindset could set in.

STOCKS POSTED A WINNING WEEK WITHOUT A NEW HIGH. Week: S&P 500 +1.21% to 7,743.41, Nasdaq 100 +3.25%, Dow +0.28% (ending a three-week losing streak); VIX 14.87. The S&P is 0.71% below its August 13 record and the Nasdaq 100 0.40% below its September 22 record. Friday: Microsoft +3.66%, Meta -3.33%.

THE WEEK AHEAD IS ALL LABOR AND INFLATION. JOLTS and consumer confidence Tuesday; ADP, August PCE and the Q2 GDP third estimate Wednesday; ISM manufacturing Thursday; September payrolls Friday 8:30, which CNBC says economists expect to roughly halve to 85,000 from 162,000, with unemployment at 4.1%. Earnings: Carnival Tuesday, Micron Wednesday after the close, Nike and Accenture Thursday.
client_frame_short: Nothing traded this weekend except Bitcoin, but the Iran story moved backward. The President publicly rejected Tehran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran's leaders answered with harder words, though no new strikes were reported. **Friday's 2% oil drop was built on deal hopes that are now off the table, so oil may open firmer Sunday night.** Underneath the headlines the picture is unchanged: a good week for stocks, a hard one for long bonds, both driven by a strong economy that costs more to finance. Nothing here calls for action; Friday's jobs report matters more than any weekend quote.
client_frame:
If a client calls about the weekend headlines, the honest answer is that the diplomacy went backward but the market has not had a chance to react yet.

What happened: Iran offered a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for a truce and sanctions relief. The President said plainly he was rejecting it, arguing Iran is 'losing so badly' and that 29 ships had crossed the strait the day before. Iran's President said his government no longer trusts talks, and a senior general said the strait stays closed until US economic pressure ends. Those are threats, not new attacks, and Iran's foreign minister says Tehran is still waiting for a formal reply - so the door is not fully shut.

Why it matters for portfolios: oil fell about 2% on Friday on hope for exactly this deal, with Brent settling at $104.32. When energy futures reopen at 6 PM Eastern tonight, some of that decline will probably come back. That is a gasoline and inflation story more than a stock story - it feeds into the Fed's thinking.

The bigger backdrop is unchanged from Friday. The S&P 500 rose 1.2% last week and the Nasdaq 100 3.25%, though neither is at a new high: the S&P is 0.71% below its August 13 record and the Nasdaq 100 0.40% below its September 22 record. The 30-year Treasury yield closed at 5.49%, its highest of 2026, and nearly all of the week's rise in yields was real rates, not inflation fear. Futures price about a 64% chance the Fed hikes again in October.

The advice stays steady. Bonds above 5% pay a real return again, which is a genuine opportunity for idle cash. Stocks are near their highs without euphoria, with the VIX at 14.87. What would change the view: a sustained oil spike back through Thursday's levels, a 10-year close above 5.25%, or a hot August PCE on Wednesday that pushes the market toward a third hike.
